General: PromptLine is a VS Code-first company building a low-latency AI pair-programmer extension targeted at product engineering teams. Key asks: sub-50ms inline suggestion RTT (aim for 40ms median), streaming completions for multi-line code expansions, and stable model pinning so behavior doesn't drift during a release.

POC & scope: 2-week pilot, 75 developer seats, instrument median/90th percentile RTT, token cost per active seat. Measure streaming warmup, KV cache hit rates, and fallback latency when hosted capacity constrained. POC plan finalized 2026-02-12; perf scripts shared.

Technical constraints: VS Code extension connects via websocket to streaming API; needs partial-edit patches (diffs) + incremental token streaming for inline suggestions. Wants SDK support for chunked edits and deterministic tokenization across client and server. Also requested per-route model pinning (pin to gpt-compat-v1.2) and automatic fallback to a quantized on-prem worker when hosted latencies exceed SLA.

Security/Compliance: Must support SSO (Okta/SAML), customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, audit logs with 1y retention, and EU data residency for some enterprise customers. SOC2 required; ISO enquiry underway.

Performance & cost: Cost sensitive — will evaluate Dedicated if unit economics for 75 seats meet targets. Concerned about per-seat rate limiting; request for fair-share token bucket and burst policies. Also asked about caching heuristics (prefix cache TTL, per-user cache isolation).

Direct quote: "We can't accept conversational-level latency — inline must feel native. If suggestions lag, adoption tanks." — L. Ahmad, CTO.

Open items: SAML metadata, perf SLA wording, rate-limit policy for per-seat fairness (tokens/min), on-prem packaging details for quantized model, explicit demo of streaming + inline suggestion UX.
